date_of_manufacture_or_packing.non_compliance_reason: Rule 6(1)(d) requires the month and year. The pack prints a purely numeric date with no month word, so dd/mm and mm/dd cannot be distinguished from the image and the month is not resolvable. Source: rules-corpus/LMPC-2011__amended-to-2021-10-31__maharashtra-compilation.pdf, Rule 6(1)(d).

unit_sale_price.non_compliance_reason: Rule 6(11) prescribes only the form of a unit sale price declaration -- 'The unit sale price shall be declared as' -- and the Rule 6(1) enumerated list (a), (aa), (b), (c), (d), (da), (e), (f), (g) carries no unit-sale-price item. The corpus therefore holds no obligation limb a deterministic rule could find in breach, so a missing declaration routes to human review rather than FAIL. Source: rules-corpus/LMPC-2011__amended-to-2021-10-31__maharashtra-compilation.pdf, Rule 6(11).

notes: A flexible pouch photographed flat on a stone surface in ordinary indoor light. This is the face bearing the full statutory panel. The pack is an imported product -- 'COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: SRI LANKA', 'IMPORTED AND PACKED BY' and 'For sale in India only.' -- so Rule 6(1)(aa) is engaged and satisfied, the only PASS on that field in this corpus. Three party blocks appear on this face: MARKETED BY, MANUFACTURED BY and IMPORTED AND PACKED BY. The bbox and raw_text frame the MANUFACTURED BY block; the other two are recorded under normalised_value.also_on_face. No unit sale price anywhere on the pack. No reference object of known size is in frame, so no millimetre letter or numeral height is measurable and no Rule 7 Table-I finding is supportable. pdp.is_measurable is false and every height field is null. The sample verdict is REVIEW for that reason alone, independently of what the declarations show.
